notes:
S1 disabled (engine=strategy2.py). 2026-08-15 session: NO PARAMETER CHANGES. Every S2 constant is owner-locked and n=11 has a win-rate sigma of ~14.5pp, so nothing in the trade record is separable from noise. Work went into MEASUREMENT and one bug.
BUG FIXED (live.py): the ghost-close path priced exits from a POLLED MID via get_price(), not from exchange fills. This is the single worst place for a mid: the position closed while the bot was DOWN, so the mid can be hours of drift from the price that actually traded, and it is written straight into journal.json and lifetime stats. The _exit_price() helper already existed and already did the right thing, but it assumed opened_at was a datetime; state.json round-trips it as an ISO STRING, so calling it from the ghost path raised AttributeError on .tzinfo, which _exit_price's own except-clause swallowed into a silent mid fallback. Hardened the helper to accept both shapes and routed the ghost path through it. Regression test in test_exit_price.py pins the since_ms handed to get_close_fill for all 5 shapes. This path is live-exercised: the bot restarts nightly ~23:05 for self-improve.
MEASUREMENT ADDED (analyze.py): two sections mined from the SCAN LOG rather than the journal, because both concern setups that never became trades - where the statistical power actually is (2765 coin-observations vs 11 trades).
  (1) ENTRY GATE CENSUS. Over 2026-08-05..08-16, of 86 RSI<=25 long candidates only 10 (11.6%) also had ADX<25; of 76 RSI>=75 short candidates only 4 (5.3%). 53.5% of long candidates sat at ADX>=40. This reproduces on live data the 92.1%/96.7% rejection figures already in memory. The mechanism is structural, not a tuning detail: an RSI extreme is CAUSED by a strong directional move, and that same move is what lifts ADX, so RSI_OVERSOLD and MAX_ADX are anti-correlated BY CONSTRUCTION. This is the binding constraint on trade frequency (0 trades in the 3 days to 08-16).
  (2) FEED HEALTH. Frozen-bar rate is now 7.9% overall, down from the 18.5% measured 2026-08-05 (mainnet 0.4%) - but the average hides the shape. It is concentrated: DOGE 24.8%, OP 13.0%, WLD 12.7%, ARB 12.3%, ATOM 10.4%, against AVAX 0.4%, SOL 0.9%, ETH 1.3%. ATOM stalled 4 consecutive hourly bars. RSI/ADX computed across repeated prices is fiction, so per-coin staleness - not the blended average - is the gate on whether constants can be re-derived yet. The clean-feed coins are re-derivable now.
FOR KAMRAN (locked, not touched): MAX_ADX=25 is the frequency bottleneck and the anti-correlation above means raising it is not a free frequency win - it deliberately buys trades in trending regimes, which is where a mean-reversion entry is most likely to be run over. If frequency must rise, the honest lever is per-coin feed quality first. Also note TRAIL_START_R is now 2.5 but the three early ratcheted winners (AVAX/ETH 08-01, BTC 08-03) locked at +1.0R/+0.75R under the OLD ratchet, so the EXIT MECHANISM meanR of +1.329 mixes two different exit regimes and understates what the current 2.5R ratchet would do. Do not read it as a forecast.
DATA (n=11, unchanged - no trades since 08-13): WR 36.4%, sumR -1.93, meanR -0.175. Avg win +1.328R, avg loss -1.034R, breakeven WR 43.8%. We sit 0.51 sigma below breakeven: not distinguishable from a working system, and not evidence of one.
